reviews.comment: Lectures were paced poorly and uninformative. No one would attend if attendance was not mandatory. Thinks what he says is profound when it is not.

If you take Thyagarajan:
1. You will have to go to class every day (participation assignments weighted super heavily)
2. He will grill you in front of the class (calls up 1 member for group projects, acts like it's the Spanish Inquisition)
3. He will make you take closed note lecture quizzes (ignoring everyone's senioritis)

I had Dr. Ravi for MEEN 402 & he was also the faculty advisor for my capstone project. Dr. Ravi was flexibile and understanding when it came to deadlines to ensure I could balance both his classwork and deliverables for my senior capstone. His lectures are interesting as he would often relate the lecture topics to his prior experience in industry.

Dr. Ravi did an excellent job teaching MEEN 402. Not only did he care about the success of our project but also took a deep interest in our own academic and personal lives. He is easily one of the best professors at TAMU, widely respected amongst other professors, and a professor I would gladly take again.

Dr Thyagarajan cares way too much about his class and thinks that everyone's life revolves around it. The lecture barely even matters but constantly calls people out in class if they aren't paying attention and makes assignments that are overly complicated or take too much time for what the class should be.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible professor that actually presents his material and how it is relevant in the real world as well as where it is being used.
